_meta.indication: Opioid analgesic indicated for the relief of moderate to severe acute pain in patients 18 years of age or older

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study KF5503/32 (Protocol R331333-PAI-3003), bunionectomy acute pain study
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active- and placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter study of multiple doses of tapentadol IR in acute pain from bunionectomy
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with at least moderate pain following bunionectomy; randomized within 9 hours post-surgery and treated for 72 hours as inpatients
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary outcome was the Summed Pain Intensity Difference over 48 hours (SPID48), based on an 11-point numerical rating scale
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo 120, Tapentadol IR 50 mg 119, 75 mg 120, 100 mg 118, Oxycodone 15 mg 125
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean SPID48 difference from placebo: 50 mg 88.2, 75 mg 113.5, 100 mg 141.4; all tapentadol doses adjusted p<0.001 vs placebo

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study KF5503/33 (Clinical Study Report R331333-PAI-3002), end-stage osteoarthritis acute pain study
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active- (oxycodone) and placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 10-day study of tapentadol IR
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with end-stage osteoarthritis of the hip or knee who were candidates for joint replacement and at Step 2 or higher of the WHO Pain Ladder
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary outcome was the 5-Day SPID, based on an 11-point numerical rating scale
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo 169, Tapentadol IR 50 mg 153, 75 mg 166, Oxycodone 10 mg 171
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean 5-Day SPID difference from placebo: 50 mg 101.2, 75 mg 97.5; adjusted p<0.001 vs placebo (no dose-response between 50 mg and 75 mg)

key_safety: Most common adverse events (≥10% in any dose group) were nausea, dizziness, vomiting and somnolence; in the pooled table nausea 30% vs 13% placebo and vomiting 18% vs 4% placebo. Safety profile is consistent with an opioid agonist; respiratory depression is the primary risk of mu-opioid agonists.
target_moa: Tapentadol is a centrally-acting synthetic analgesic; analgesic efficacy is thought to be due to mu-opioid agonist activity and inhibition of norepinephrine reuptake

rems.type: A REMS was required; it consists of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of REMS assessments, due to tapentadol's serious risks and high potential for abuse

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened because tapentadol is a member of a previously approved class of opioid drugs and the product did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues beyond its class

description.text: Pediatric exclusivity determination supplement fulfilling a Written Request for pediatric information in patients birth to <17 years for management of moderate to severe acute pain

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application, containing a request for Pediatric Exclusivity Determination, was submitted to fulfill the requirements of a Written Request issued by the Agency on July 8, 2013, with amendments issued on August 14, 2014, June 22, 2015, July 10, 2019, December 2, 2021, and November 3, 2023, to obtain pediatric information on Nucynta (tapentadol) from birth (i.e., neonates) to less than 17 years of age for the management of moderate to severe acute pain. Related labeling changes were previously incorporated in the approval letter for sNDA-024 dated July 3, 2023.

summary.text: Standard NDA (505(b)) approved on November 20, 2008 based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials; no advisory committee was convened; a REMS (Medication Guide) was required and the FDA review recommended that a Schedule II classification under the Controlled Substances Act should be adequate to mitigate the risk of abuse.

citations.quote: tapentadol, which is not currently scheduled under the Controlled Substances Act, was approved on November 20, 2008, with labeling that refers to CSA scheduling.

I recommend approval for tapentadol HCL IR for the management of acute moderate-to-severe pain in adults. Efficacy was demonstrated at doses of 50mg, 75mg, and 100mg, using a dosing interval of every 4 to 6 hours in two adequate and well-controlled clinical trials.

Standard pharmacovigilance and a Schedule II classification should be adequate to mitigate the risk of abuse for this product. Should signals of abuse be found postmarketing, more extensive risk management strategies may need to be implemented. A REMS has been required due to the need for a MedGuide to inform patients of the risks associated with the use of tapentadol.
